unresolved: TWO ARCHUNIT RULES ARE DISABLED IN odata-filter-spring-boot-starter'S ArchitectureTest, as named debt with the reason at the point of the disable. (1) cycles.modules-are-free-of-cycles - 16 violations across roughly eleven distinct cycles, rooted in config -> core -> policy -> config and core <-> validation <-> policy. They pre-date the module having any architecture test, which is why nobody had seen them. (2) configuration-properties.configuration-properties-are-validated - ODataFilterProperties carries no @Validated, and the one-annotation fix needs a validation implementation this module deliberately does not have. Both are handed to the change fix-odata-filter-package-cycles, whose proposal and design are written; its deliverable is re-enabling them.

A CYCLE I INTRODUCED IN THE PREVIOUS CHANGE was found here and fixed here: ODataQueryExecutor in querydsl depended on ODataFilterService in core while core already depended on querydsl. add-odata-query-execution's receipt should be read together with this one - it reported that change complete without this defect, because the module had no ArchUnit runner to catch it.

THE MODULE HAD NO ARCHITECTURE TEST AT ALL before this change, so the whole shared rule library - not only the audit group - had never been applied to ru.ludwigandreas.odatafilter. Adding the runner is how the new rule became load-bearing, and it is also how the debt above became visible. Worth checking how many other library modules are in the same position; this change deliberately did not look.

THE NEW RULE WAS WRONG ON ITS FIRST WRITING and a compliant module caught it, not a test of mine: file-action's constants class and Lombok's generated builder both tripped it. Narrowed to top-level records. The two evasions it still cannot catch are renaming the package and declaring the event as a class instead of a record; both are named in the rule's javadoc.

FLAKY TEST in a module this change does not touch: pat-spring-boot-starter's PatDirectAuthenticationIT$FilterEnabled.revokedTokenStopsWorking failed the second clean install with StaleObjectStateException on PatEntity - an optimistic-locking conflict between a last-use timestamp update and the revoke. It passed on a targeted rerun, on a full module verify and in the third clean install. Nothing was changed to make it pass, so it is still flaky.

LATENT DEFECT, still not fixed (web-core): WebCoreLocalizationAutoConfiguration's ValidationMessageConfiguration is conditional on the jakarta.validation API rather than on an implementation. It is why odata-filter excludes that transitive jar and why ODataFilterProperties cannot simply be annotated @Validated. Fixing it is a web-core change with sixteen dependents; recorded in add-odata-query-execution's receipt as well.

LATENT DEFECT, still not fixed (odata-filter): odataFilterProblemMapper and odataFilterProblemMessageBundle are @Bean methods with @ConditionalOnClass whose return types reference web-core's optional ExceptionProblemMapper - the shape that failed for the springdoc customizer last change. Their own test passes with web-core filtered out, so they were left alone again.

ENVIRONMENT, not a code defect: Maven defaults to Homebrew JDK 26 here and JaCoCo 0.8.12 cannot instrument class file major version 70, so every build in this change was run with JAVA_HOME pointing at the installed Temurin 17.
